result.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
result.summary: Trustworthiness is a crucial issue for generative AI, as modern models can produce convincing and confident responses even when their outputs are incomplete, unsupported, or wrong. The frequent absence of ground-truth knowledge or labels complicates verification of generative AI outputs. To address this issue, we propose a trustworthiness framework grounded in model-internal confidence calibrated against an external expert reference. We estimate per-token trustworthiness of a student generative model as the statistical typicality of each generated token relative to an expert model's distribution, where the expert is used as a distributional reference rather than as a source of factual verification labels. To this end, we introduce an AI ontology calibrator that leverages the student model's internal latent features and token-level output statistics to compute expert-reference acceptance scores. Combined with traditional token-level confidence, entropy, and perplexity statistics, calibrator scores yield a compact set of $15$ response-level indicators for correctness classification. Evaluated across BF program generation, mathematical problem solving, and medical question answering, combined calibrator and traditional indicators provide complementary reliability signal which could be used to build detectors of untrustworthy outputs and hallucinations. Remarkably, our experiments show that these detectors are transferable across domains, although transferability is not always symmetric.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出以专家模型分布为参照、结合学生模型内部 latent 特征与 token 级输出统计的「AI ontology calibrator」，估计逐 token 可信度，并与置信度、熵、困惑度组成 15 个响应级指标用于正确性与幻觉检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用内部 latent 特征做逐 token 可靠性校准的思路，可能可供核查能否用作 latent 推理状态的可靠性诊断或停止判据；但该工作仅在纯文本任务上评估，跨模态推理迁移性尚不明确。
